summary: Created a local root CA named "OS Comparison Root CA" (4096-bit RSA, self-signed, 10-year validity) on node1, installed it as a trusted system CA via update-ca-certificates, and verified trust with openssl. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native reboot, polled until SSH returned, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart), and re-verified the CA cert and its trust status survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04 Xenial) and confirmed availability of openssl, update-ca-certificates, and sudo
Generated 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 CA cert with CN=OS Comparison Root CA (10yr validity) at /etc/ssl/os-comparison-ca/
Copied the CA cert to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/os-comparison-root-ca.crt and ran update-ca-certificates ('1 added')
Verified the cert is linked into /etc/ssl/certs/ and openssl verify trusts it against /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
Captured baseline boot_id on node1 before restart
Issued shutdown -r now via backgrounded sudo command so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until SSH/exec became available again post-reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving a genuine restart occurred
Re-verified post-reboot that the CA cert file, its /etc/ssl/certs symlink, and openssl trust verification all remained intact

evidence.requirement: Local CA 'OS Comparison Root CA' created
evidence.summary: Generated RSA key and self-signed cert; openssl x509 shows subject=issuer=/CN=OS Comparison Root CA with valid 2026-2036 date range

evidence.requirement: CA cert installed as trusted system CA
evidence.summary: update-ca-certificates reported '1 added, 0 removed'; openssl verify against system CA bundle returned OK, and byte-for-byte diff confirms the installed cert matches the generated one
Captured boot_id f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; command returned ACK_REBOOT_ISSUED immediately

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: SSH connection refused mid-reboot, then boot_id came back as 9028230f-c5ad-4710-b5c3-1a3559db6ed0, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of CA trust configuration/data
evidence.summary: After reboot, cert file and /etc/ssl/certs symlink still present, byte-identical to original, and openssl verify still returns OK
